title: Why would God love me?
theme: Do you struggle to believe Jesus loves you personally? A Catholic reflection on God's unconditional love, feelings of unworthiness, Psalm 105, and Luke 11:27–28.
opening: We are told that Jesus loves us so deeply He would have given His life for even one of us. But what happens when we believe in His love and still struggle to believe that we are worthy of receiving it?
prayer: Heavenly Father,  You created me in Your image and likeness, and through Your Son, Jesus Christ, You have revealed the depth of Your love for me.  Forgive me for the times I allow my wounds and feelings of unworthiness to overshadow what You have already made known. Help me to remember Your promises, to trust Your Word, and to receive the love You so freely give.  When I struggle, draw me closer. When I fall, remind me of Your mercy. And when I question my worth, help me remember that I am Your beloved child.  May Your love become the foundation of my faith, the strength in my struggles, and the peace that carries me through each day.  Amen.
body:
Have you ever struggled to believe that Jesus loves you personally? Not simply that He loves humanity, or that He died for the sins of the world, but that His love for you is so great that He would have given His life for you alone?

I have heard this said many times, and although I believe in Jesus and His infinite love, I have struggled for years to fully accept that truth.

Today, during prayer, that struggle returned. I prayed, and I cried. How could Jesus love me that much? How could I possibly be worthy of such love?

I imagine I am not alone in asking these questions.

While searching for understanding, I visited the website of St. Michael's Center for Spiritual Renewal and came across a prayer called *I Am Loved*. Two passages spoke directly to what I had been struggling with.

“I know that I am beloved because I have been created in the image and likeness of God.”

And then:

“I know that I am beloved because God the Father has sent His Son Jesus Christ into the World because of that love.”

Such simple words, yet how easily we forget what they mean.

We were created in God's image and likeness. Before we accomplished anything, before we could prove ourselves worthy, God already loved us. And out of that love, He sent His Son into the world. Jesus did not give His life for an anonymous multitude. He knew and loved each person for whom He suffered.

And that includes you. That includes me.

Then I turned to today's readings, and there was the reassurance I had been searching for.

In Psalm 105, we hear:

“Look to the LORD in his strength; seek to serve him constantly. Recall the wondrous deeds that he has wrought.”

*Recall.*

What a powerful instruction when we begin to question what we know to be true.

God does not ask us to find new proof of His love each time we struggle. He invites us to remember what He has already done. His love was revealed through the life, death, and Resurrection of Jesus Christ.

And in today's Gospel, Jesus tells us:

“Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and observe it.”

There is something important in those words. Jesus does not say blessed are those who never doubt, never struggle, or always feel worthy. He speaks of those who hear God's Word and live according to it.

And if God's Word tells us that we are loved, shouldn't we learn to trust that truth, even when our hearts struggle to accept it?

Sometimes our experiences in life leave wounds that make love difficult to receive. We may understand God's love in our minds, yet struggle to allow that same truth to settle within our hearts.

But His love is not dependent upon our feelings. It does not diminish when we struggle, nor does it disappear when we fall.

Perhaps that is part of our spiritual journey: learning to trust what God has revealed rather than allowing our wounds to determine what we believe about ourselves.

I know there will still be moments when I cry, when I feel unworthy, or when old wounds resurface. But those moments do not change what Christ has done for me.

And this is why remaining close to Him matters so much. Through prayer, Scripture, and the sacraments, we continually return to the truth of His love. We seek His strength, receive His mercy, and strive to remain in communion with Him, ready for the day He calls us home.

Today I was reminded that faith is not always about discovering something new. Sometimes it is about finally allowing ourselves to believe what God has been telling us all along.

**I may still struggle to feel worthy of His love, but I do not have to question whether His love is real.**

And neither do you.
